question.prompt:
The grading scale shown is used at Jones Junior High. The fifteen scores in Mr. Freeman’s class were: \(89,\) \(72,\) \(54,\) \(97,\) \(77,\) \(92,\) \(85,\) \(74,\) \(75,\) \(63,\) \(84,\) \(78,\) \(71,\) \(80,\) \(90.\)

\[\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{A} & 93\text{--}100\\ \hline \text{B} & 85\text{--}92\\ \hline \text{C} & 75\text{--}84\\ \hline \text{D} & 70\text{--}74\\ \hline \text{F} & 0\text{--}69\\ \hline\end{array}\]

In Mr. Freeman’s class, what percent of the students received a grade of C?

solutions.explanation:
A grade of C includes scores from \(75\) through \(84\), including both endpoints. Checking the fifteen scores against that range gives exactly
\[
75,\ 77,\ 78,\ 80,\ 84.
\]
These are five students. To find their percentage of the class, divide this count by the total number of students:
\[
\frac{5}{15}=\frac13.
\]
Therefore the percentage receiving C is
\[
\frac13\cdot100\%=33\frac13\%,
\]
choice D.
solutions.title: Count the C scores and find their percentage
